text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT -> host gpu-rt12-024 (10.40.24.18) fired at 1798887776. Reason: kernel panic (XID 79) followed by kubelet NotReady. Auto-escalation level: P1. Auto-ack rules: 10m to first ack. /links: https://pd.redwood.example/INC12345

oncall_maya: acked — I'm on it. landing on the host now. pinging infra. :phone:

infra_jake: on my way to the rack IRL (will be ~4m). can you confirm node ownership? gpu-rt12-024 is in prod-gpu-pool-4, running model-serving-v2.

oncall_maya: confirmed. traffic shows immediate 503s for some model shards. routing still has fallback to smaller replica but p95 client latency spiked. customer-facing impact: observed ~1.2% error rate across region for the last 2 mins. tagging oncall-sre.

sre_ana: joining. can you paste pod list? I want to see which replicas were on that host.

eng_luis: that host had 3 pods: model-serve-v2-6, model-serve-v2-7, batch-infer-12. two of those were on the critical path.

oncall_maya: running quick checks:
```
# ssh jump -> host (using serial)
ssh root@gpu-rt12-024
dmesg | tail -n 40
# output: kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
# kubelet status: systemctl status kubelet -> dead / not responding
```

incident-bot: Auto-note: Serial console log captured and uploaded to https://logs.redwood.example/serial/gpu-rt12-024/1798887776.

infra_jake: nvme errors reported too on the host, looks like IO stall before panic. NVMe SMART shows increased media errors on nvme1. ordering an immediate SOC-level RMA if we can't revive.

sre_ana: can we cordon + drain the node to avoid further scheduling? 

oncall_maya: doing cordon now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-rt12-024.rw-prod
kubectl drain gpu-rt12-024.rw-prod --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m
```
oncall_maya: drain started, some pods stuck terminating (node unresponsive). fallback routing in place for live traffic, but batch jobs may be impacted.

eng_luis: adding a note for customer support: some long-running batch jobs on v2 may restart later; small % of online queries may have higher latency while repopulating caches.

ops-bot: Metric alert: prod-gpu-pool-4 request_errors increased 1.2% -> triggered. p95 latency increased from 120ms -> 780ms in the last 2m.

sre_ana: if drain can't finish due to kubelet dead, we should force delete pods after confirming replicas spun up elsewhere. I'll watch replica counts.

oncall_maya: replica status: model-serve-v2 has 6/8 replicas ready after fallback, autoscaler triggered a burst. More margin now but one shard lost.

infra_jake: trying a soft power-cycle via BMC to recover nvme/controller. If that doesn't bring kubelet back within 3 mins, we'll tag host for RMA and evict permanently.

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation to SRE lead in 6m if not acknowledged by lead.

sre_ana: assigning postmortem owner: @sre_ana. I'm collecting logs: kernel oops + nvme SMART -> probably hardware. tagging for cross-team: @infra_jake, @eng_luis.

oncall_maya: customers impacted: small percentage of inference requests in region; I recommend communication to trust ops if this persists beyond 15m.

infra_jake: BMC reports host responded to power cycle and came up to POST; kernel panic persisted and landed back in same XID; controller reported firmware timeout. RMA path initiated: ticket INF-RMA-783.

oncall_maya: handoff plan: I'll stay for the next 10m to confirm traffic normalization, then hand to night oncall. If any remaining 503s after 15m, escalate to infra RMA lead and trigger customer notif.

eng_luis: quick mitigation note — we can temporarily increase routing weight to regional spare nodes to reduce latency while replacements arrive. Doing that now.

sre_ana: thanks team. Summary for timeline: 1) 1798887776 pager fired (kernel panic XID 79) -> 2) cordon/drain attempted -> 3) BMC power-cycle failed to fully recover -> 4) nvme firmware/driver suspected -> 5) RMA initiated. Postmortem owner: @sre_ana. Customer impact: ~1.2% request errors for ~10m, degraded p95 for ~5-10m.

oncall_maya: leaving a final note before handoff: cluster routing stabilized, error rate dropping to 0.15% at 1798888050. handing to night: @infra_jake (oncall), @sre_ana (postmortem). :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread auto-closed for active ack by oncall at 1798888060.
